blockingFindings.title: Official setup can exceed the plugin source limit
blockingFindings.issue: ensureSetupOfficialPresetState() checks plugin.sources.length > MAX_PLUGIN_SOURCES before adding the official source, but if the config already has exactly MAX_PLUGIN_SOURCES entries and no official source, it pushes one more entry and writes the over-limit config.
blockingFindings.suggestion: In ensureSetupOfficialPresetState(), before pushing a new official source, reject when plugin.sources.length >= MAX_PLUGIN_SOURCES, or validate the source count again before writeProjectConfig().
blockingFindings.rationale: R9 requires setup candidate and official preset handling to enforce source-count bounds. This path can persist a config that violates the bound and then fail later when the registry is loaded.

blockingFindings.title: Plugin contribution paths can escape the plugin root
blockingFindings.issue: readPluginJson() bounds file type and size, but callers still build metadata paths with path.join(manifest.root, entry.path, ...), config.schema, and config.defaults without verifying that the resolved path remains inside the plugin root.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Add a helper that resolves contribution metadata paths against manifest.root and rejects paths outside that root, then use it in PluginManifest.presetEntries() and loadPluginConfigDefaults() before calling readPluginJson().
blockingFindings.rationale: R9 includes path/file bounds for plugin metadata. Without containment checks, plugin metadata can reference small JSON files outside the package and have setup treat them as trusted preset or config metadata.
